outcome: Outcome of delivery (assisted delivery rate, C-section rate, labor stage duration)
Maternal complications (nausea, vomiting, low back pain, headache, urinary incontinence and retention, dizziness, drowsiness)
cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women experiencing labor.
finding: Epidural analgesia was not associated with a higher assisted delivery rate or C-section rate, nor significant maternal or fetal heart rate complications, and was associated with a shorter labor stage.
mod_finding: Epidural analgesia was not associated with a higher assisted delivery rate or higher rate of C-section.
